It's dangerous due to primary and secondary voltage as well as danger of destroying the ignition system.

Never start the engine after removal of distributor cap and/or disconnection of wire on ignition coil term. 4 - pull off plug on ignition control unit.

Replace distributor cap and/or rotor.

What are the 5 steps in the troubleshooting procedure?
The 5 steps are: 1. Verify the Problem, 2. Analyze the Problem, 3. Isolate the Problem, 4. Repair the Problem, 5. Check the Problem.
What tools are required for isolating problems according to step 3 of the troubleshooting procedures?
Isolating the problem requires the use of a voltmeter and/or ohmmeter. A voltmeter measures voltage at selected points in a circuit.
Why should you disconnect the car battery when using an ohmmeter?
You should disconnect the car battery when using an ohmmeter because the battery voltage will cause the ohmmeter logic to give false readings.
What resistance values are shown in the voltage test diagram?

How should you connect a voltmeter to take a voltage measurement?

To take a voltage measurement, connect the negative lead of the voltmeter to the battery's negative terminal or other known good ground. Then connect the positive lead of the voltmeter to the point you want to test.
What warning is given about using an ohmmeter on solid-state components?
Do not use an ohmmeter on solid-state components. The voltage that the ohmmeter applies to the circuit could damage these components.
What does an ohmmeter measure in a circuit?
An ohmmeter measures a circuit's resistance to current flow. It has an internal battery that provides current to the circuit under test.
What components are labeled in the voltage test diagram?
The voltage test diagram shows a Power Distribution Box, Low Fluid Switch, Voltmeter, and Low Fluid Indicator.
What should you do in step 1 of the troubleshooting procedure?
In step 1, you should operate the problem circuit to check the accuracy of the complaint and note the symptoms of the inoperative circuit.
What is recommended for efficient troubleshooting when isolating problems?
Keep in mind that a logical simple procedure is the key to efficient troubleshooting. Test for the most likely cause of failure first. Try to make tests at points which are easily accessible.

What are the possible causes if my clutch is slipping?

Clutch slipping can be caused by: insufficient clutch contact pressure, seriously worn liner, liner splattered with oil from transmission or crankshaft seal faults, overheated clutch, or clutch not being an original BMW part.
How do I fix a clutch that slips due to insufficient contact pressure?
Replace clutch 21 21 000.
What should I do if the clutch grabs but the liner is not as specified?

My clutch won't release - what could cause the drive plate to be seized on the transmission input shaft?
The drive plate can seize on the transmission input shaft, which requires servicing the drive plate and transmission input shaft, replacing damaged parts if necessary.

What causes clutch noise due to unbalanced clutch and drive plate?

What are the possible causes when the transmission shifts hard or makes sticking and scratching noises?

The causes include insufficient clutch release due to inadequate pedal travel, worn drive plate, seized liner on flywheel, seized drive plate on transmission input shaft, defective bearing for transmission input shaft in crankshaft, air in clutch hydraulic system, thick viscous transmission oil, damaged bushes for selector rod arrest, excessive play in shift lever mount, worn selector forks, or worn sliding sleeve.
How do you correct insufficient clutch pedal travel?
Check pedal travel and adjust if necessary. Remove excessively thick floor mats. Floor clutch pedal when changing gear 35 31 000.
What should you do if the transmission grabs when shifting?

Check for insufficient clutch release or worn synchromesh rings/sliding sleeve. If clutch release is the issue, see the corrections listed above. For worn synchromesh components, check synchronization and replace damaged parts using procedure 23 23 503.
What causes a transmission to be loud during operation?

A loud transmission can be caused by oil level being too low, defective transmission shaft bearings, damaged gears, defective needle bearing of output or input shaft, or defective bearing for transmission input shaft in crankshaft.
How do you fix worn selector forks?

What should I check if I find oil on the clutch bell housing?

What should I check if the ABS control lamp comes on immediately after starting the engine?
Check pin 16 on ABS wire harness plug for ground contact. The possible causes are hydraulic control unit operating voltage or power supply issues, or the acceleration sender has ground contact.

The cause is a break in the 'idle speed boost' current path. Check for a break in connection between ABS wire harness plug pin 3 and solenoid ground.
What causes the ABS control lamp to stay on at high engine speed of a stopped car or longer lasting ABS control after stopping the car?
The cause is dispersion in sensor wire. Check routing of wires for ABS sensors.

What are the main components of the ABS system?
The ABS consists of a control unit, hydraulic unit, speed sensors and a wire harness.
Where is the electronic control unit located?
The electronic control unit is located in the passenger compartment below the instrument panel on the left-hand side.
How do the speed sensors work to detect wheel movement?

Each speed sensor has a gear wheel, which runs past the permanently magnetized edge of the speed sensor and is installed in the wheel hub. The rotary motion of the wheels is recorded by inductive sensors and an electric signal is sent to the electronic control unit.
Where is the hydraulic unit located and what is its purpose?

The hydraulic unit is located in the engine compartment and was added to the conventional brake system. To control the brake pressure in the wheel brake cylinders, the brake hydraulic unit has the three-way valves which permit three brake pressure conditions.
What are the three brake pressure phases that the hydraulic unit controls?

Pressure build-up, pressure holding and pressure drop. These three pressure phases adapt themselves in the sequences and length to the requirements of the desired control characteristic and power flow between the road surface and tyre.
What happens when the ABS control unit detects a defect in the wire harness or electrical part?

If the control unit detects a defect in the wire harness or electrical part of the equipment, the monitoring circuit will switch off the ABS and guarantees normal use of the brake system. An ABS indicator lamp reports this condition to the driver.
What is the tightening torque for front brake disc installation?

How should brake disc thickness be measured when checking for runout and thickness difference?
Mount a dial gauge holder and check lateral runout of the brake disc with a dial gauge. Measure difference in thickness within the braking surface at about 8 points with a micrometer.
What are the requirements before checking front brake disc runout?
The requirement is that wheel bearings must be okay before performing the runout check.
What is the important rule about grinding brake discs?
Always fine grind both sides of both brake discs on one axle. After machining to minimum thickness, install only one more set of brake pads.
How is the brake disc secured to the hub?
Mount the brake disc with two M 12 x 1.5 bolts as noted in the installation procedure.
What must be done if only one brake disc needs replacement?
Even if only one brake disc has to be replaced, always replace both brake discs of one axle.
What callout numbers are visible in the brake disc removal procedure?

Wear protective clothing! Absolute cleanliness is required for the performance of work on an air conditioner.
